title: Power profiles daemon
description: The power-profiles-daemon module displays the active power-profiles-daemon profile and cycle through the available profiles on click.

placeholders.description: Icon (from format-icons) representing the active profile.
The CPU driver reported by recent power-profiles-daemon versions. (tooltip)
The platform driver reported by recent power-profiles-daemon versions. (tooltip)
Kept for backward compatibility: resolves to the legacy single driver on older daemons and falls back to the CPU driver on recent ones. (tooltip)

format.label: What to show
format.doc: Message displayed on the bar. {icon} and {profile} are respectively substituted with the icon representing the active profile and its full name.
format.description: The text shown in the bar. Words in curly braces, like {icon}, are replaced with live values: see the list of placeholders.

tooltip-format.label: Tooltip text
tooltip-format.doc: Messaged displayed in the module tooltip. {icon} and {profile} are respectively substituted with the icon representing the active profile and its full name. {cpu_driver} and {platform_driver} are substituted with the CPU and platform drivers reported by recent power-profiles-daemon versions. {driver} is kept for backward compatibility: it resolves to the legacy single driver on older daemons and falls back to the CPU driver on recent ones.
tooltip-format.description: What the popup shows. It uses the same placeholders as the bar text.

tooltip.label: Show tooltip
tooltip.description: Show a small popup with more details when the mouse is over the module.

format-icons.label: Icons
format-icons.default_note: See default value in the example below.
format-icons.doc: Icons used to represent the various power-profile. Note: the default configuration uses the font-awesome icons. You may want to override it if you don't have this font installed on your system.
format-icons.description: The icons used for {icon}. When it is a list, the first icon is used for the lowest level and the last one for the highest.

expand.label: Fill empty space
expand.doc: Enables this module to consume all left over space dynamically.
expand.description: Stretch the module to use all the free space left in its section.
